     runbook: |
-      The concurrency 44 and 56 points of the GB300 AgentX disaggregated lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3.1-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#5069](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5069)). Dynamo + vLLM run one prefill worker and five (or three) decode workers, each TP8 + DCP8 across two 4-GPU GB300 trays. The prefill worker also runs the routed experts EP8 on MegaMoE; the decode workers use no expert parallelism and run the low-latency decode backend. KV moves from prefill to decode over NIXL, and all workers share an RDMA Mooncake store in host DRAM. The lane ran the image digest the preset pins (vLLM `0.1.dev25356+gdbbc9e310`), Dynamo built from `229be5cff1156859b0e3e43b598ee800b2f81ccc` ([`v1.7.0-kimi-k3.1-pro-dev.1`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/v1.7.0-kimi-k3.1-pro-dev.1), which registers the K3.1 model type) and Mooncake `0.3.14`; the preset has been measured only on that combination, with the preview draft `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview`.
+      The concurrency 44 and 104 points of the GB300 AgentX disaggregated lane in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) (`kimik3.1-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg`, [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#5109](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/5109)). Dynamo + vLLM run one prefill worker and five decode workers, each TP8 + DCP8 across two 4-GPU GB300 trays (48 GPUs). The prefill worker also runs the routed experts EP8 on MegaMoE; the decode workers use no expert parallelism and run the low-latency decode backend. KV moves from prefill to decode over NIXL, and all workers share an RDMA Mooncake store in host DRAM. The lane ran the image digest the preset pins (vLLM `0.1.dev25380+gf4c96184b`), Dynamo built from `ec06c09e7232e24f6faeec4069acdc61e4379916` (the source of Dynamo's `1.8.0.dev20261119` nightly) and Mooncake `0.3.14`; the preset has been measured only on that combination.
 
-      | Clients | Prefill workers | Decode workers | GPUs | Decode `--max-num-seqs` | Decode capture sizes |
-      |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
-      | 44, 56 | 1 | 5 | 48 | 64 | 5 to 320 in steps of 5 |
-      | 56 | 1 | 3 | 32 | 256 | 5 to 320 in steps of 5, then 340 to 1280 in steps of 20 |
+      | Clients | Prefill workers | Decode workers | GPUs | Draft tokens | Decode capture sizes | Prefill chunking |
+      |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
+      | 44 | 1 | 5 | 48 | 5 | 6 to 384 in steps of 6 | default |
+      | 104 | 1 | 5 | 48 | 4 | 5 to 320 in steps of 5 | `--long-prefill-token-threshold 4096`, adaptive |
 
       Each point renders one prefill worker and one decode worker; start the table's number of workers per role with the same commands, two trays each. Run every worker command on both of its trays with the same `--master-addr` (the first tray's address), `--nnodes 2` and `--node-rank 0` or `1`.
 
       **Serving config.**
-      - **Prefill:** TP8 + DCP8 with `--enable-expert-parallel` and `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `--max-num-seqs 32`, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs for 4 to 8192 tokens. `--kernel-config '{"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}'` runs the sparse indexer's top-k on the DeepSelect kernels instead of the image's default chain. `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1` turns on the fused GEMM + reduce-scatter. `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_LIMIT` and `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_WAITING_LIMIT` set Dynamo's admission limits for the prefill engine to 1024 requests each.
-      - **Decode:** TP8 + DCP8 without expert parallelism, with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=0`. `--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'` runs pure decode steps on the fused low-latency path; the Low-latency decode toggle is not offered under PD, so the preset sets the flag in the decode args. `--use-replayssm` makes KDA verification replay the accepted prefix instead of keeping one recurrent state per draft token. The decode `--compilation-config` sets only the capture sizes (multiples of 5 rows: 1 + 4 draft tokens per request) and replaces the PD strategy's `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, so the CUDA graph mode is vLLM's default, as in the lane.
-      - **Both roles:** FP8 MLA KV cache with an MXFP4 indexer key cache (`indexer_kv_dtype`) and BF16 indexer logits (`indexer_logits_dtype`; K3.1 defaults to FP32); FP32 KDA conv and recurrent state (`--mamba-cache-dtype float32 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32`), as the K3.1 precision policy requires; the A2A DCP backend and the direct DCP all-to-all and gather paths (`VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_*`); prefix caching with `--prefix-match-unit 128`; `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, `--enable-cumem-allocator`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` and `--stream-interval 10`. Both roles pin `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1`: left unset, NIXL P/D raises the DCP KV interleave after the specialized decode has read it.
-      - **Spec decoding** (on in this preset) uses the K3.1 DSpark draft [`Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark-preview) with 4 tokens, probabilistic drafting and block rejection.
+      - **Prefill:** TP8 + DCP8 with `--enable-expert-parallel` and `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `--max-num-seqs 32`, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs for 4 to 8192 tokens. `--kernel-config '{"sparse_indexer_topk_backend":"deep_select"}'` runs the sparse indexer's top-k on the DeepSelect kernels instead of the image's default chain. `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=1` turns on the fused GEMM + reduce-scatter. `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_LIMIT` and `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_WAITING_LIMIT` set Dynamo's admission limits for the prefill engine to 1024 requests each. At 104 clients, `--long-prefill-token-threshold 4096 --long-prefill-token-threshold-adaptive` caps a long prompt's chunk next to other requests, so short follow-up turns do not queue behind it.
+      - **Decode:** TP8 + DCP8 without expert parallelism, with `VLLM_ENABLE_GEMM_RS=0` and `--max-num-seqs 64`. `--additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'` runs pure decode steps on the fused low-latency path; the Low-latency decode toggle is not offered under PD, so the preset sets the flag in the decode args. `--use-replayssm` makes KDA verification replay the accepted prefix instead of keeping one recurrent state per draft token. The decode `--compilation-config` sets only the capture sizes (multiples of 1 + draft tokens per request, up to 64 requests) and replaces the PD strategy's `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, so the CUDA graph mode is vLLM's default, as in the lane.
+      - **Opt-in decode paths:** the decode env turns on the image's opt-in TP8 + DCP8 decode paths, all off by default (`K31_*`): specialized decode steps at 5 to 40 rows, KDA and attention kernels, one-pass decode prep and fused draft layers. At 44 clients, `K31_S30K=6` selects the specialized decode table for 6-row requests (5 draft tokens). They exist only in the image the preset pins.
+      - **Both roles:** FP8 MLA KV cache with an MXFP4 indexer key cache (`indexer_kv_dtype`) and BF16 indexer logits (`indexer_logits_dtype`; K3.1 defaults to FP32); FP32 KDA conv and recurrent state (`--mamba-cache-dtype float32 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32`), as the K3.1 precision policy requires; the A2A DCP backend and the direct DCP all-to-all and gather paths (`VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_*`); prefix caching with `--prefix-match-unit 1408`, the KV block of the draft's sliding-window group at TP8 + DCP8 (with any other unit, vLLM turns off partial prefix-cache hits for the whole hybrid KV cache); `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, `--enable-cumem-allocator`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` and `--stream-interval 10`. Both roles pin `--cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1`: left unset, NIXL P/D raises the DCP KV interleave after the specialized decode has read it.
+      - **Spec decoding** (on in this preset) uses the K3.1 DSpark draft [`Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark) at revision `e4e6e626` (5 GQA layers, 2,048-token sliding window), with probabilistic drafting and block rejection: 5 draft tokens at 44 clients, 4 at 104.
       - **Collectives and kernels:** FlashInfer all-reduce stays on (`VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER=1`); NCCL symmetric memory and the sharded sequence-parallel shared expert stay off (`VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0`, `VLLM_KIMI_K3_SHARD_SP_SHARED_EXPERT=0`), and so do TOKENSPEED_MLA's FP16 partials (`TOKENSPEED_MLA_FP16_PARTIALS=0`). NCCL runs over the NVLink domain (`NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1`, `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1`, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`, `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL`) without a network plugin (`NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none`).
       - **KV transfer:** NIXL uses `UCX_MEMTYPE_REG_WHOLE=n` and `UCX_TCP_AF_PRIO=inet`. The Mooncake transfer engine uses `MC_SLICE_SIZE=1048576`, `MC_MAX_MR_SIZE=4294967296` and `MC_ENABLE_DEST_DEVICE_AFFINITY=1`, and `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0` for hosts without the nvidia-peermem module. vLLM loads from the store with 4 receive threads (`VLLM_MOONCAKE_LOAD_RECV_THREADS=4`), and `VLLM_MOONCAKE_STORE_SELECTIVE_LEASE=1` makes a store lookup lease only the keys that a hit loads.
       - **Timeouts and housekeeping:** `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600` (from the recipe's Blackwell settings), `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800`, `VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT=600000`, `DYN_TCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=120` and `ETCD_LEASE_TTL=600`. A store lookup may take up to 60 s (`lookup_timeout_s`; the connector's default is 1 s), and starts when the request arrives, with up to 16 lookups in flight (`lookup_prefetch_limit`) and results kept for 30 s (`lookup_prefetch_ttl_s`). `TILELANG_CLEANUP_TEMP_FILES=1` removes TileLang's temporary build files. Every worker loads the checkpoint with `--load-format fastsafetensors`, which changes load time only.

       ```bash
+      # 104 clients

       ```

+# Training and Reinforcement Learning (RL)
+
+vLLM is widely used as the high-throughput rollout and teacher-scoring engine for post-training workflows including RLHF, GRPO, Online DPO, and on-policy distillation.
+
+## Quick Routing Guide (Task → Doc)
+
+| What you want to do | Document | Key Flags / APIs |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Synchronize updated trainer weights into a running vLLM engine (IPC, NCCL, M2N, Sharded RDT, ModelExpress) | [Weight Updates](weight_updates/README.md) | `--weight-transfer-config`, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE` |
+| Understand in-place weight reload vs. layerwise reload & online quantization (QeRL) | [Direct Weight Reload](weight_updates/direct_reload.md) / [Layerwise (Re)loading](weight_updates/layerwise.md) | `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=auto\|direct\|layerwise` |
+| Verify that a weight update landed identically on every rank | [Weight Checker](weight_updates/weight_checker.md) | SHA-256 parameter digest check |
+| Export rollout artifacts to the trainer (MoE routing, sampling masks, teacher top-K logprobs) | [Rollout Artifacts](rollout_artifacts/README.md) | `--enable-return-routed-experts`, `prompt_logprob_token_ids` |
+| Overlap rollout generation and training (async RL / one-off pipelining) | [Async Reinforcement Learning](async_rl.md) | `pause_generation`, `resume_generation`, `weight_version` |
+| Integrate vLLM with Hugging Face TRL | [Transformers Reinforcement Learning (TRL)](trl.md) | `use_vllm=True`, `vllm_mode` |
+
+## Related Features Across vLLM
+
+These capabilities live under `docs/features/` because they also serve general inference, but are frequently used in RL and post-training setups:
+
+- **[Sleep Mode](../features/sleep_mode.md)**: Free GPU memory (weights and KV cache) between rollout and training phases in colocated RL.
+- **[Batch Invariance](../features/batch_invariance.md)**: Reduce train–inference numerical mismatch by making rollout outputs invariant to batching.
+- **[Online Quantization](../features/quantization/online.md)**: Quantize full-precision trainer weights on the fly during [direct](weight_updates/direct_reload.md#online-quantization) or [layerwise](weight_updates/layerwise.md#layerwise-loading-with-online-quantization) reload.
+- **[Hidden State Extraction](../features/speculative_decoding/extract_hidden_states.md)**: Export per-token hidden states via a connector for training speculative-decoding draft models (e.g., EAGLE).
+
+## Open-Source RL Libraries Using vLLM
+
+The following open-source RL libraries use vLLM for fast rollouts (sorted alphabetically and non-exhaustive):
+
+- [Cosmos-RL](https://github.com/nvidia-cosmos/cosmos-rl)
+- [ms-swift](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift/tree/main)
+- [NeMo-RL](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/RL)
+- [Open Instruct](https://github.com/allenai/open-instruct)
+- [OpenRLHF](https://github.com/OpenRLHF/OpenRLHF)
+- [PipelineRL](https://github.com/ServiceNow/PipelineRL)
+- [Prime-RL](https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-rl)
+- [SkyRL](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL)
+- [TRL](https://github.com/huggingface/trl) (see [TRL integration guide](trl.md))
+- [Unsloth](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth)
+- [verl](https://github.com/volcengine/verl)

+# Rollout Artifacts
+
+During RL rollouts and on-policy distillation, the trainer often needs auxiliary per-token outputs from the inference pass—beyond just generated token IDs—to eliminate train–inference mismatch or compute distillation targets.
+
+## Quick Routing Guide
+
+| Artifact | Document | Use Case | Key Flag / Parameter |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| **Routed Experts (R3)** | [Routed Experts Return](routed_experts.md) | MoE routing replay: reuse rollout router expert IDs during the training forward pass | `--enable-return-routed-experts` |
+| **Sampling Mask** | [Sampling Mask](sampling_mask.md) | Distribution replay: return the exact token IDs that survived top-k / top-p / min-p filtering | `--return-sampling-mask`, `--logprobs-mode processed_logprobs` |
+| **Prompt Token ID Logprobs** | [Prompt Token ID Logprobs](prompt_token_id_logprobs.md) | On-policy distillation (teacher scoring): compute teacher logprobs for exact student top-K candidate tokens | `prompt_logprob_token_ids` |
+| **Hidden States** | [Hidden State Extraction](../../features/speculative_decoding/extract_hidden_states.md) | Export hidden states via connector for training speculative-decoding draft models (e.g., EAGLE) | `kv_transfer_params` / hidden states connector |
+
+## Auxiliary Output Connector (`aux_output_connector`)
+
+For large per-token artifacts such as MoE routed experts, vLLM uses the **aux output connector** (`vllm/distributed/aux_output_connector/`) to store artifact rows per engine in host memory, keyed by KV block hash, on the engine's first tensor-parallel worker. See [Routed Experts Return — Row storage](routed_experts.md#row-storage) for storage layout, replica affinity, cache invalidation on weight updates, and `max_bytes` sizing.

 """Normalized configuration consumed by native offloading backends."""
 
+from __future__ import annotations
+
 from collections.abc import Mapping
 from dataclasses import dataclass
+from enum import Enum
 from typing import Any
 
 
+class OffloadAccessMode(Enum):
+    """Direction(s) in which an offloading connector may transfer data.
+
+    Configured through the optional `access_mode` key of a connector's
+    config: `read` serves loads but never accepts stores, `write` accepts
+    stores but never serves loads, and `readwrite` (the default) does both.
+    """
+
+    READ = "read"
+    WRITE = "write"
+    READWRITE = "readwrite"
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_config(cls, value: str | OffloadAccessMode | None) -> OffloadAccessMode:
+        """Parse a configured `access_mode` value, defaulting to `readwrite`."""
+        if value is None:
+            return cls.READWRITE
+        if isinstance(value, cls):
+            return value
+        if not isinstance(value, str):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"access_mode must be a string, got {type(value).__name__}: {value!r}"
+            )
+        try:
+            return cls(value.strip().lower())
+        except ValueError:
+            valid = ", ".join(repr(access_mode.value) for access_mode in cls)
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Invalid access_mode {value!r}; expected one of {valid}"
+            ) from None
+
+    @property
+    def can_read(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the connector may serve loads (read from the tier)."""
+        return self is not OffloadAccessMode.WRITE
+
+    @property
+    def can_write(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the connector may accept stores (write to the tier)."""
+        return self is not OffloadAccessMode.READ
+

@@ -0,0 +1,362 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Low-M BF16 tensor-core projections for SM120/SM121: batched `x @ w.T` with
+deterministic split-K for narrow outputs, and a grouped q/k/v projection."""
+
+import functools
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import num_compute_units
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import current_stream
+
+MAX_M = 16
+_MP = 16
+_MAX_TILES = 4096
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _ll_gemm_kernel(
+    X,
+    W,
+    Bias,
+    Y,
+    P,
+    C,
+    M,
+    N,
+    K,
+    SXB,
+    SXM,
+    SWB,
+    SWN,
+    SYB,
+    SYM,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+    K_PER_SPLIT: tl.constexpr,
+    SPLIT: tl.constexpr,
+    MP: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Program `(n, b, s)` computes column tile `n` of batch `b` over K range
+    `s`. With `SPLIT > 1` it writes fp32 partials to `P` `[SPLIT, B, MP, N]`;
+    the last of the tile's programs to finish (counted in `C`, reset to 0
+    after) sums them in split order, so results are deterministic."""
+    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()
+    pid_n = tl.program_id(0)
+    b = tl.program_id(1)
+    s = tl.program_id(2)
+    rows = tl.arange(0, MP)
+    cols = pid_n * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    ks = s * K_PER_SPLIT + tl.arange(0, BK)
+    x_ptrs = X + (b * SXB + rows[:, None] * SXM + ks[None, :])
+    w_ptrs = W + (b * SWB + cols[None, :] * SWN + ks[:, None])
+    acc = tl.zeros((MP, BN), tl.float32)
+    for _ in range(0, tl.minimum(K - s * K_PER_SPLIT, K_PER_SPLIT), BK):
+        # Issuing W's copies before X's measured faster.
+        w = tl.load(w_ptrs, (cols[None, :] < N) & (ks[:, None] < K), other=0)
+        x = tl.load(x_ptrs, (rows[:, None] < M) & (ks[None, :] < K), other=0)
+        acc += tl.dot(x, w)
+        x_ptrs += BK
+        w_ptrs += BK
+        ks += BK
+
+    is_last = True
+    if SPLIT > 1:
+        num_b = tl.num_programs(1)
+        tile = b * tl.num_programs(0) + pid_n
+        offs = rows[:, None] * N + cols[None, :]
+        mask = (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols < N)[None, :]
+        tl.store(P + ((s * num_b + b) * MP * N + offs), acc, mask)
+        tl.debug_barrier()
+        is_last = tl.atomic_add(C + tile, 1, sem="acq_rel", scope="gpu") == SPLIT - 1
+        if is_last:
+            acc = tl.zeros((MP, BN), tl.float32)
+            for i in tl.static_range(SPLIT):
+                acc += tl.load(
+                    P + ((i * num_b + b) * MP * N + offs),
+                    mask,
+                    cache_modifier=".cg",
+                )
+            tl.atomic_xchg(C + tile, 0, sem="relaxed", scope="gpu")
+    if is_last:
+        if Bias is not None:
+            acc += tl.load(Bias + cols, cols < N, other=0).to(tl.float32)[None, :]
+        tl.store(
+            Y + (b * SYB + rows[:, None] * SYM + cols[None, :]),
+            acc.to(Y.dtype.element_ty),
+            (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < N),
+        )
+    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_launch_dependents()
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _segment_input(b, XQ, XK, XV, SXQ, SXK, SXV):
+    if b == 0:
+        x, stride = XQ, SXQ
+    elif b == 1:
+        x, stride = XK, SXK
+    else:
+        x, stride = XV, SXV
+    return x, stride
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _qkv_bmm_kernel(
+    XQ,
+    XK,
+    XV,
+    W,
+    Y,
+    M,
+    N,
+    K,
+    S1,
+    S2,
+    SXQ,
+    SXK,
+    SXV,
+    SWN,
+    SYM,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+    MP: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Columns `[0, S1)` of `Y` are `XQ @ W.T`, `[S1, S2)` `XK` and `[S2, N)`
+    `XV`. A tile spanning a boundary runs both inputs' dots and picks per
+    column (the second input's loads hit L2)."""
+    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()
+    n0 = tl.program_id(0) * BN
+    n1 = tl.minimum(n0 + BN, N) - 1
+    b_lo = (n0 >= S1).to(tl.int32) + (n0 >= S2).to(tl.int32)
+    b_hi = (n1 >= S1).to(tl.int32) + (n1 >= S2).to(tl.int32)
+    x_lo, sx_lo = _segment_input(b_lo, XQ, XK, XV, SXQ, SXK, SXV)
+    x_hi, sx_hi = _segment_input(b_hi, XQ, XK, XV, SXQ, SXK, SXV)
+    rows = tl.arange(0, MP)
+    cols = n0 + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    ks = tl.arange(0, BK)
+    x_lo += rows[:, None] * sx_lo + ks[None, :]
+    x_hi += rows[:, None] * sx_hi + ks[None, :]
+    w_ptrs = W + (cols[None, :] * SWN + ks[:, None])
+    acc_lo = tl.zeros((MP, BN), tl.float32)
+    acc_hi = tl.zeros((MP, BN), tl.float32)
+    for _ in range(0, K, BK):
+        x_mask = (rows[:, None] < M) & (ks[None, :] < K)
+        w = tl.load(w_ptrs, (cols[None, :] < N) & (ks[:, None] < K), other=0)
+        acc_lo += tl.dot(tl.load(x_lo, x_mask, other=0), w)
+        acc_hi += tl.dot(tl.load(x_hi, x_mask, other=0), w)
+        x_lo += BK
+        x_hi += BK
+        w_ptrs += BK
+        ks += BK
+    segment = (cols >= S1).to(tl.int32) + (cols >= S2).to(tl.int32)
+    acc = tl.where((segment == b_lo)[None, :], acc_lo, acc_hi)
+    tl.store(
+        Y + (rows[:, None] * SYM + cols[None, :]),
+        acc.to(Y.dtype.element_ty),
+        (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < N),
+    )
+    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_launch_dependents()
+
+
+class _Config(NamedTuple):
+    bn: int
+    bk: int
+    split: int
+    k_per_split: int
+    num_warps: int
+    num_stages: int
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _config(nb: int, n: int, k: int) -> _Config:
+    """Split K into about one wave of programs when that gives at least 3
+    splits, preferring 16-column tiles; otherwise one 32-column tile over all
+    of K."""
+    num_sms = num_compute_units()
+    bk = min(128, max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(k)))
+    k_tiles = triton.cdiv(k, bk)
+    for bn in (16, 32):
+        split = min(32, k_tiles, num_sms // (nb * triton.cdiv(n, bn)))
+        if split >= 3:
+            tiles_per_split = triton.cdiv(k_tiles, split)
+            split = triton.cdiv(k_tiles, tiles_per_split)
+            return _Config(bn, bk, split, tiles_per_split * bk, 4, 4)
+    bk = min(256, max(16, triton.next_power_of_2(k)))
+    return _Config(32, bk, 1, triton.cdiv(k, bk) * bk, 4, 3)
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _counter(stream: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Split-K tile counters for one stream; each launch leaves them zeroed."""
+    return torch.zeros(_MAX_TILES, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+
+def _ll_gemm(
+    x: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None, out: torch.Tensor
+) -> None:
+    nb, m, k = x.shape
+    n = w.shape[1]
+    assert 0 < m <= MAX_M and w.shape == (nb, n, k)
+    assert x.stride(2) == w.stride(2) == 1
+    assert bias is None or (bias.shape == (n,) and bias.stride(0) == 1)
+    assert out.shape == (nb, m, n) and out.stride(2) == 1
+    assert max(nb * w.stride(0), nb * x.stride(0), nb * out.stride(0)) < 2**31
+    cfg = _config(nb, n, k)
+    n_tiles = triton.cdiv(n, cfg.bn)
+    partials = counter = None
+    if cfg.split > 1:
+        assert nb * n_tiles <= _MAX_TILES
+        partials = torch.empty(
+            (cfg.split, nb, _MP, n), dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device
+        )
+        counter = _counter(current_stream().cuda_stream)

+        out,

+        counter,
+        m,

+        k,
+        x.stride(0),
+        x.stride(1),
+        w.stride(0),
+        w.stride(1),
+        out.stride(0),
+        out.stride(1),
+        BN=cfg.bn,
+        BK=cfg.bk,
+        K_PER_SPLIT=cfg.k_per_split,
+        SPLIT=cfg.split,
+        MP=_MP,
+        num_warps=cfg.num_warps,
+        num_stages=cfg.num_stages,
+        launch_pdl=True,
+    )
+
+
+def use_qkv_bmm(
+    x_q: torch.Tensor, x_k: torch.Tensor, x_v: torch.Tensor, w: torch.Tensor
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether `qkv_bmm` serves bf16 `x_q`, `x_k`, `x_v` `[M, K]` and `w`."""
+    return (
+        x_q.is_cuda
+        and x_q.ndim == 2
+        and 0 < x_q.shape[0] <= MAX_M
+        and x_q.shape == x_k.shape == x_v.shape
+        and x_q.dtype == x_k.dtype == x_v.dtype == w.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and x_q.stride(1) == x_k.stride(1) == x_v.stride(1) == w.stride(1) == 1
+        and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)
+    )
+
+
+def qkv_bmm(
+    x_q: torch.Tensor,
+    x_k: torch.Tensor,
+    x_v: torch.Tensor,
+    w: torch.Tensor,
+    k_start: int,
+    v_start: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """One launch of three linears on consecutive row ranges of `w` `[N, K]`:
+    output columns `[0, k_start)` from `x_q`, `[k_start, v_start)` from `x_k`
+    and the rest from `x_v`, each `[M, K]` with M <= 16. Returns `[M, N]`
+    with fp32 accumulation."""
+    xs = (x_q, x_k, x_v)
+    m, k = x_q.shape
+    n = w.shape[0]
+    s1, s2 = k_start, v_start
+    bn = 32
+    assert 0 < m <= MAX_M and w.shape == (n, k)
+    assert all(x.shape == (m, k) and x.stride(1) == 1 for x in xs)
+    assert w.stride(1) == 1 and s1 > 0 and s1 + bn <= s2 <= n  # one boundary per tile
+    assert max(n * w.stride(0), *(m * x.stride(0) for x in xs)) < 2**31
+    out = torch.empty((m, n), dtype=x_q.dtype, device=x_q.device)
+    # About 1.6 waves of 32-column tiles at Inkling's 8608 columns; wider
+    # tiles or split-K measured no faster.
+    _qkv_bmm_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, bn),)](
+        x_q,
+        x_k,
+        x_v,
+        w,
+        out,
+        m,
+        n,
+        k,
+        s1,
+        s2,
+        x_q.stride(0),
+        x_k.stride(0),
+        x_v.stride(0),
+        w.stride(0),
+        out.stride(0),
+        BN=bn,
+        BK=128,
+        MP=_MP,
+        num_warps=4,
+        num_stages=4,
+        launch_pdl=True,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+def sm12x_bf16_ll_gemm(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    out_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Low-latency `x @ weight.T` (+ `bias` `[N]`) for at most `MAX_M` rows,
+    with fp32 accumulation, into `out` if given. `weight` `[N, K]` takes `x`
+    `[..., K]` -> `[..., N]`; `weight` `[B, N, K]` takes `x` `[B, M, K]` ->
+    `[B, M, N]`."""
+    n = weight.shape[-2]
+    if weight.ndim == 3:
+        if out is None:
+            out = x.new_empty((*x.shape[:2], n), dtype=out_dtype or x.dtype)
+        _ll_gemm(x, weight, bias, out)
+        return out
+    lead = x.shape[:-1]
+    x2 = x.reshape(-1, x.shape[-1])
+    if out is None:
+        out = x.new_empty((x2.shape[0], n), dtype=out_dtype or x.dtype)
+    if x2.shape[0]:
+        _ll_gemm(x2[None], weight[None], bias, out[None])
+    return out.view(*lead, n)
+
+
+def use_sm12x_bf16_ll_gemm(
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None = None
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether `sm12x_bf16_ll_gemm` serves these operands."""
+    if weight.ndim == 2:
+        shapes_ok = x.ndim >= 2
+        m = x.numel() // max(x.shape[-1], 1)
+    else:
+        shapes_ok = weight.ndim == 3 and x.ndim == 3 and x.shape[0] == weight.shape[0]
+        m = x.shape[-2] if x.ndim >= 2 else 0
+    return (
+        shapes_ok
+        and x.is_cuda
+        and weight.device == x.device
+        and x.dtype == weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and x.shape[-1] == weight.shape[-1]
+        and x.stride(-1) == weight.stride(-1) == 1
+        and 0 < m <= MAX_M
+        and (
+            bias is None
+            or (
+                bias.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+                and bias.device == x.device
+                and bias.stride(0) == 1
+            )
+        )
+        and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)
+    )

+def _record_moe_routing(model: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+    """Redraw the routers (dummy weights route every token alike) and the
+    loop message controllers (dummy ones leave every pass alike), then
+    record, in call order, the torch reference routing of every MoE call's
+    input (sorted expert ids per token)."""
+    from vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.loop import Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer
+    from vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.moe import Inkling2MoE
+    from vllm.models.inkling2.nvidia.ops.linear import linear_k_groups
+    from vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug import gpu_sync_allowed
+
+    calls: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    model.routing_calls = calls
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+
+    def hook(moe: Inkling2MoE, args: tuple) -> None:
+        gate = moe.gate
+        logits = linear_k_groups(args[0].contiguous(), gate.weight)
+        ids = torch.topk(logits.sigmoid() + gate.bias, gate.topk).indices
+        # The test's own reference copy; CI runs with VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error.
+        with gpu_sync_allowed():
+            calls.append(ids.sort(-1).values.cpu())
+
+    for module in model.modules():
+        if isinstance(module, Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer):
+            # Unit-scale gates: tanh(gain), tanh(forget) ~ O(1).
+            down, gain_forget = module.controller_down, module.controller_gain_forget
+            down.normal_(std=down.shape[-1] ** -0.5, generator=generator)
+            gain_forget.normal_(std=gain_forget.shape[-1] ** -0.5, generator=generator)
+        if isinstance(module, Inkling2MoE):
+            module.gate.weight.normal_(generator=generator)
+            module.gate.bias.zero_()
+            module.register_forward_pre_hook(hook)
+
+
+def _routing_calls(model: torch.nn.Module) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
+    return model.routing_calls

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Looped Inkling2 checkpoints (`loop_config`).
+
+The core layers `[core_start, core_end)` run `num_passes` times: a prelude,
+then each pass from the AttnRes state after the prelude, then the coda from
+the last pass's state. Each pass of a core layer has its own KV and
+conv-state caches. In passes after the first, every core sublayer input
+(attention q/k/v and MLP) is blended with a message: a normalized-value
+AttnRes read of the previous pass's blocks, merged by a gated low-rank
+controller. Each sublayer's short conv runs fused with the next AttnRes mix
+(and small batches at TP > 1 with its all-reduce); without sequence parallel.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from vllm.distributed import tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce
+
+from ..configs import Inkling2ModelConfig
+from ..quant_config import Inkling2QuantConfig
+from .model import (
+    Inkling2DecoderLayer,
+    Inkling2ForConditionalGeneration,
+    Inkling2Model,
+)
+from .ops.attn_res import attn_res
+from .ops.linear import linear_k_groups
+from .ops.loop import blend_rms_norm, pair_rms_norm
+from .sconv import conv_metadata
+
+LOOP_STREAMS = ("attn", "k", "v", "mlp")
+
+
+class Inkling2MessageController(nn.Module):
+    """Blends a loop message into a core sublayer input: from the rank-`r`
+    projection `h` of the RMS-normalized `[dest, message]`,
+    `(1 - tanh(forget(h))) * dest + tanh(gain(h)) * message` in fp32.
+
+    The weights are views of the layer's stream-stacked weights
+    (`Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer`), which run every stream at once; `forward`
+    is the per-stream reference.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, down: torch.Tensor, gain: torch.Tensor, forget: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.down_weight = nn.Parameter(down, requires_grad=False)
+        self.gain_weight = nn.Parameter(gain, requires_grad=False)
+        self.forget_weight = nn.Parameter(forget, requires_grad=False)
+
+    def forward(self, dest: torch.Tensor, message: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """fp32 `(T, D)` `dest` and `message` -> fp32 `(T, D)`."""
+        pair = torch.stack((dest, message), dim=1)
+        pair = pair * torch.rsqrt(pair.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-6)
+        normalized = pair.to(torch.bfloat16).flatten(1)
+        hidden = linear_k_groups(normalized, self.down_weight, torch.bfloat16)
+        gain = torch.mm(hidden, self.gain_weight.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)
+        forget = torch.mm(hidden, self.forget_weight.t(), out_dtype=torch.float32)
+        return (1.0 - torch.tanh(forget)) * dest + torch.tanh(gain) * message
+
+
+class Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer(Inkling2DecoderLayer):
+    """A loop core layer: per-pass caches and a message controller per
+    stream (`LOOP_STREAMS`), whose weights are stacked over the streams."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Inkling2ModelConfig,
+        layer_id: int,
+        quant_config: Inkling2QuantConfig | None,
+        prefix: str,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(
+            config, layer_id, quant_config, prefix, num_passes=config.num_loop_passes
+        )
+        assert config.loop_config is not None
+        rank, width = config.loop_config["gate_rank"], config.hidden_size
+        streams = len(LOOP_STREAMS)
+        # down (S, r, 2D) and [gain; forget] (S, 2D, r), bf16.
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "controller_down",
+            torch.empty(streams, rank, 2 * width, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            persistent=False,
+        )
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "controller_gain_forget",
+            torch.empty(streams, 2 * width, rank, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            persistent=False,
+        )
+        self.controllers = nn.ModuleDict(
+            {
+                stream: Inkling2MessageController(
+                    self.controller_down[i],
+                    self.controller_gain_forget[i, :width],
+                    self.controller_gain_forget[i, width:],
+                )
+                for i, stream in enumerate(LOOP_STREAMS)
+            }
+        )
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self) -> None:
+        # The controllers' weights must still alias the stacked ones.
+        for i, controller in enumerate(self.controllers.values()):
+            down, gain_forget = self.controller_down, self.controller_gain_forget
+            assert controller.down_weight.data_ptr() == down[i].data_ptr()
+            assert controller.gain_weight.data_ptr() == gain_forget[i].data_ptr()
+
+    def blend(
+        self,
+        streams: slice,
+        dest: torch.Tensor,
+        message: torch.Tensor,
+        norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+        norm_eps: float,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """The `streams` controllers on fp32 `(S, T, D)` `dest` (may
+        broadcast over streams) and `message`, each output RMS-normalized
+        with its row of `norm_weight` `(S, D)`: bf16 `(S, T, D)`."""
+        pair = pair_rms_norm(dest, message)
+        hidden = torch.bmm(pair, self.controller_down[streams].transpose(1, 2))
+        gain_forget = torch.bmm(
+            hidden,
+            self.controller_gain_forget[streams].transpose(1, 2),
+            out_dtype=torch.float32,
+        )
+        return blend_rms_norm(dest, message, gain_forget, norm_weight, norm_eps)
+
+
+class Inkling2LoopModel(Inkling2Model):
+    seq_parallel_paths = False
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: Inkling2ModelConfig,
+        quant_config: Inkling2QuantConfig | None,
+        prefix: str,
+    ) -> None:
+        # Serving options set through --hf-overrides skip the constructor.
+        config.check_loop_options()
+        super().__init__(config, quant_config, prefix)
+        self.loop_core = config.loop_core_layers
+        self.hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+        # Message pseudo-queries (raw), two per core layer: attn/mlp and k/v.
+        shape = (2 * len(self.loop_core), config.hidden_size)
+        self.middle_cycle_cross_pass_queries = nn.Parameter(
+            torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.float32), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        self.middle_cycle_cross_pass_kv_queries = nn.Parameter(
+            torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.float32), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        # Per core layer, the `LOOP_STREAMS` queries scaled by D**-0.5.
+        self.register_buffer(
+            "message_queries",
+            torch.zeros(
+                len(self.loop_core),
+                len(LOOP_STREAMS),
+                config.hidden_size,
+                dtype=torch.float32,
+            ),
+            persistent=False,
+        )

+    def process_weights_after_loading(self) -> None:
+        queries = self.middle_cycle_cross_pass_queries.view(-1, 2, self.hidden_size)
+        kv_queries = self.middle_cycle_cross_pass_kv_queries.view(
+            -1, 2, self.hidden_size
+        )
+        # (attn, k, v, mlp) = (queries[0], kv[0], kv[1], queries[1]).
+        stacked = torch.stack(
+            (queries[:, 0], kv_queries[:, 0], kv_queries[:, 1], queries[:, 1]), 1
+        )
+        self.message_queries.copy_(stacked * self.hidden_size**-0.5)

+    def _make_layer(

+        config: Inkling2ModelConfig,
+        layer_id: int,
+        quant_config: Inkling2QuantConfig | None,
+        prefix: str,

+        if layer_id in config.loop_core_layers:
+            return Inkling2LoopDecoderLayer(config, layer_id, quant_config, prefix)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Low-M BF16 tensor-core projections for SM120/SM121."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+MAX_M = 16
+_BN, _BK = 32, 256
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gemv_kernel(
+    X,
+    W,
+    B,
+    Y,
+    M,
+    N,
+    K,
+    SX,
+    SW,
+    SY,
+    HAS_BIAS: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+    MP: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    pid = tl.program_id(0)
+    cols = pid * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    rows = tl.arange(0, MP)
+    acc = tl.zeros((MP, BN), tl.float32)
+    for k0 in range(0, K, BK):
+        ks = k0 + tl.arange(0, BK)
+        w = tl.load(
+            W + cols[None, :].to(tl.int64) * SW + ks[:, None],
+            (cols[None, :] < N) & (ks[:, None] < K),
+            other=0,
+        )
+        x = tl.load(
+            X + rows[:, None] * SX + ks[None, :],
+            (rows[:, None] < M) & (ks[None, :] < K),
+            other=0,
+        )
+        acc += tl.dot(x, w)
+    if HAS_BIAS:
+        acc += tl.load(B + cols, cols < N, other=0).to(tl.float32)[None, :]
+    tl.store(
+        Y + rows[:, None] * SY + cols[None, :],
+        acc.to(Y.dtype.element_ty),
+        (rows[:, None] < M) & (cols[None, :] < N),
+    )
+
+
+def sm12x_bf16_gemv(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    out_dtype: torch.dtype | None = None,
+    out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    lead = x.shape[:-1]
+    x2 = x.reshape(-1, x.shape[-1])
+    m, k = x2.shape
+    assert m <= MAX_M
+    n = weight.shape[0]
+    if out is None:
+        out = torch.empty((m, n), device=x.device, dtype=out_dtype or x.dtype)
+    if m:
+        _gemv_kernel[(triton.cdiv(n, _BN),)](
+            x2,
+            weight,
+            bias,
+            out,
+            m,
+            n,
+            k,
+            x2.stride(0),
+            weight.stride(0),
+            out.stride(0),
+            HAS_BIAS=bias is not None,
+            BN=_BN,
+            BK=_BK,
+            MP=16,
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+    return out.view(*lead, n)
+
+
+def use_sm12x_bf16_gemv(
+    x: torch.Tensor, weight: torch.Tensor, bias: torch.Tensor | None = None
+) -> bool:
+    return (
+        x.is_cuda
+        and weight.device == x.device
+        and x.dtype == weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+        and x.ndim >= 2
+        and weight.ndim == 2
+        and x.shape[-1] == weight.shape[1]
+        and x.stride(-1) == weight.stride(-1) == 1
+        and 0 < x.numel() // x.shape[-1] <= MAX_M
+        and (
+            bias is None
+            or (
+                bias.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+                and bias.device == x.device
+                and bias.stride(0) == 1
+            )
+        )
+        and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Loop message controllers, batched over streams.
+
+A controller blends a fp32 message into a fp32 sublayer input `dest`: from
+`h = down(rms([dest, message]))` (bf16), `out = (1 - tanh(forget(h))) * dest +
+tanh(gain(h)) * message` in fp32, unfused as the reference. The output feeds
+the sublayer's RMSNorm, applied in the same kernel.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, tldevice, triton
+
+from .norm import rsqrt
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _pair_rms_norm_kernel(
+    Dest,
+    Message,
+    Out,
+    stride_dest_s,
+    T,
+    eps,
+    D: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    s = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    t = tl.program_id(1).to(tl.int64)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = cols < D
+    dest = tl.load(Dest + s * stride_dest_s + t * D + cols, mask, other=0)
+    message = tl.load(Message + (s * T + t) * D + cols, mask, other=0)
+    dest_rstd = rsqrt(tl.div_rn(tl.sum(dest * dest), D) + eps)
+    message_rstd = rsqrt(tl.div_rn(tl.sum(message * message), D) + eps)
+    out = Out + (s * T + t) * (2 * D)
+    tl.store(out + cols, (dest * dest_rstd).to(Out.dtype.element_ty), mask)
+    tl.store(out + D + cols, (message * message_rstd).to(Out.dtype.element_ty), mask)
+
+
+def pair_rms_norm(dest: torch.Tensor, message: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """bf16 `(S, T, 2D)` `[rms(dest), rms(message)]` of fp32 `(S, T, D)`
+    inputs, weightless; `dest` may broadcast over streams (stride 0)."""
+    num_streams, num_tokens, d = message.shape
+    assert dest.shape == message.shape and message.is_contiguous()
+    assert dest.stride(1) == d and dest.stride(2) == 1
+    assert dest.dtype == message.dtype == torch.float32
+    out = message.new_empty((num_streams, num_tokens, 2 * d), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    if num_tokens:
+        _pair_rms_norm_kernel[(num_streams, num_tokens)](
+            dest,
+            message,
+            out,
+            dest.stride(0),
+            num_tokens,
+            1e-6,
+            D=d,
+            BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(d),
+            num_warps=8,
+        )
+    return out
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _blend_rms_norm_kernel(
+    Dest,
+    Message,
+    GainForget,
+    NormW,
+    Out,
+    stride_dest_s,
+    stride_w_s,
+    T,
+    norm_eps,
+    D: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    s = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    t = tl.program_id(1).to(tl.int64)
+    cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = cols < D
+    row = s * T + t
+    dest = tl.load(Dest + s * stride_dest_s + t * D + cols, mask, other=0)
+    message = tl.load(Message + row * D + cols, mask, other=0)
+    gain = tldevice.tanh(tl.load(GainForget + row * (2 * D) + cols, mask, other=0))
+    forget = tldevice.tanh(
+        tl.load(GainForget + row * (2 * D) + D + cols, mask, other=0)
+    )
+    x = (1.0 - forget) * dest + gain * message
+    rstd = rsqrt(tl.div_rn(tl.sum(x * x), D) + norm_eps)
+    y = x * rstd
+    y = y * tl.load(NormW + s * stride_w_s + cols, mask, other=0).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(Out + row * D + cols, y.to(Out.dtype.element_ty), mask)
+
+
+def blend_rms_norm(
+    dest: torch.Tensor,
+    message: torch.Tensor,
+    gain_forget: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_eps: float,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """bf16 `(S, T, D)` RMSNorm (row `s` of `norm_weight` `(S, D)`) of
+    `(1 - tanh(forget)) * dest + tanh(gain) * message`, with fp32 `(S, T, D)`
+    `dest` (may broadcast over streams) and `message`, and fp32 `(S, T, 2D)`
+    `gain_forget` = `[gain, forget]`. `norm_weight` may broadcast too."""
+    num_streams, num_tokens, d = message.shape
+    assert dest.shape == message.shape and message.is_contiguous()
+    assert dest.stride(1) == d and dest.stride(2) == 1
+    assert gain_forget.shape == (num_streams, num_tokens, 2 * d)
+    assert gain_forget.is_contiguous() and gain_forget.dtype == torch.float32
+    assert norm_weight.shape == (num_streams, d) and norm_weight.stride(1) == 1
+    out = message.new_empty((num_streams, num_tokens, d), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    if num_tokens:
+        _blend_rms_norm_kernel[(num_streams, num_tokens)](
+            dest,
+            message,
+            gain_forget,
+            norm_weight,
+            out,
+            dest.stride(0),
+            norm_weight.stride(0),
+            num_tokens,
+            norm_eps,
+            D=d,
+            BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(d),
+            num_warps=8,
+            # The blend is unfused (no FMA), as the reference.
+            enable_fp_fusion=False,
+        )
+    return out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""SM12 Humming NVFP4 GEMMs using Inkling's quantized expert rows."""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.moe_align_block_size import (
+    moe_align_block_size,
+)
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+from .block_scales import _scale_offsets
+from .moe_sm90 import HummingExperts
+from .trtllm_bmm import ExpertPlan
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _prepare_rows(
+    Scales,
+    Tiles,
+    OutScales,
+    Ids,
+    GROUPS: tl.constexpr,
+    TILE: tl.constexpr,
+    MAX_CTAS: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    tile = row // TILE
+    active = tile < tl.load(Tiles + 2 * MAX_CTAS)
+    row_end = tl.load(Tiles + MAX_CTAS + tile, active, other=0)
+    valid = active & (row < row_end)
+    expert = tl.load(Tiles + tile, active, other=-1)
+    tl.store(Ids + row, tl.where(valid, expert, -1))
+    groups = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    scales = tl.load(
+        Scales + _scale_offsets(row, groups, GROUPS, TILE),
+        valid & (groups < GROUPS),
+        other=0,
+    )
+    tl.store(OutScales + row * GROUPS + groups, scales, groups < GROUPS)
+
+
+class HummingNVFP4Experts(HummingExperts):
+    """Keep quantized activations and their outer scales across both GEMMs.
+
+    Weight outer scales are already folded into the routed row scales, so the
+    prepared weights use unit global scales. Repacking preserves FP4 payloads
+    and E4M3 scale bytes; the existing router and SiTU quantizer remain in use.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, weights, shapes) -> None:
+        from vllm.utils.humming import ModeloptNvfp4InputSchema
+
+        super().__init__(
+            weights,
+            shapes,
+            nvfp4=True,
+            input_schema=ModeloptNvfp4InputSchema(
+                quant_algo="NVFP4", dynamic=True
+            ).to_humming_schema(torch.bfloat16),
+        )
+
+    def bmm(
+        self,
+        quantized: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor],
+        name: str,
+        tiles: torch.Tensor,
+        plan: ExpertPlan,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from vllm.utils.humming import humming_forward
+
+        act, scale, row_scale = quantized
+        config, tensors = self.configs[name], self.tensors[name]
+        rows, groups = act.shape[0], config.shape_k // 16
+        scales = torch.empty((rows, groups), device=act.device, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        ids = torch.empty((rows, 1), device=act.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+        _prepare_rows[(rows,)](
+            scale.view(torch.uint8),
+            tiles,
+            scales,
+            ids,
+            GROUPS=groups,
+            TILE=plan.tile,
+            MAX_CTAS=plan.max_ctas,
+            BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(groups),
+        )
+        sorted_ids, expert_ids, count = moe_align_block_size(
+            ids,
+            self._block_m(name, rows),
+            self.num_experts,
+            ignore_invalid_experts=True,
+        )[:3]
+        return humming_forward(

+            inputs=act,
+            weight=tensors["weight"],
+            weight_scale=tensors["weight_scale"],
+            weight_scale_2=tensors["weight_scale_2"],

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""SM120/121 expert GEMMs with native NVFP4 MMA and dequantized MXFP8.
+
+Weights remain row-major, while activations retain Inkling2's tile-padded
+R8c4/R128c4 layout and its four-or-six quantization and outer row scales.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+
+from .block_scales import _scale_offsets
+from .trtllm_bmm import ExpertPlan
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _expert_gemm(
+    Act,
+    ActScale,
+    RowScale,
+    Weight,
+    WeightScale,
+    ExpertScale,
+    Out,
+    Tiles,
+    MAX_CTAS: tl.constexpr,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    TILE: tl.constexpr,
+    BM: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    tile = tl.program_id(0)
+    if tile >= tl.load(Tiles + 2 * MAX_CTAS):
+        return
+    expert = tl.load(Tiles + tile).to(tl.int64)
+    row_end = tl.load(Tiles + MAX_CTAS + tile)
+    rows = tile * TILE + tl.program_id(1) * BM + tl.arange(0, BM)
+    valid = rows < tl.minimum(row_end, (tile + 1) * TILE)
+    cols = tl.program_id(2) * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BM, BN), tl.float32)
+    for k in range(tl.cdiv(K, BK)):
+        packed = k * (BK // 2) + tl.arange(0, BK // 2)
+        groups = k * (BK // 16) + tl.arange(0, BK // 16)
+        a = tl.load(
+            Act + rows[:, None].to(tl.int64) * (K // 2) + packed[None, :],
+            valid[:, None] & (packed[None, :] < K // 2),
+            other=0,
+        )
+        a_scale = tl.load(
+            ActScale + _scale_offsets(rows[:, None], groups[None, :], K // 16, TILE),
+            valid[:, None] & (groups[None, :] < K // 16),
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        w = tl.load(
+            Weight + (expert * N + cols[None, :]) * (K // 2) + packed[:, None],
+            (cols[None, :] < N) & (packed[:, None] < K // 2),
+            other=0,
+        )
+        w_scale = tl.load(
+            WeightScale + (expert * N + cols[:, None]) * (K // 16) + groups[None, :],
+            (cols[:, None] < N) & (groups[None, :] < K // 16),
+            other=0.0,
+        )
+        acc = tl.dot_scaled(a, a_scale, "e2m1", w, w_scale, "e2m1", acc)
+    acc *= tl.load(ExpertScale + expert)
+    acc *= tl.load(RowScale + rows, valid, other=0)[:, None]
+    tl.store(
+        Out + rows[:, None].to(tl.int64) * N + cols[None, :],
+        acc,
+        valid[:, None] & (cols[None, :] < N),
+    )
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _dequant_e4m3(values, exponents):
+    exponents = exponents.to(tl.uint32)
+    scales = tl.where(exponents == 0, 0x00400000, exponents << 23)
+    scales = scales.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+    return (values.to(tl.float32) * scales).to(tl.bfloat16)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _expand_scales(scales):
+    rows: tl.constexpr = scales.shape[0]
+    groups: tl.constexpr = scales.shape[1]
+    scales = tl.broadcast_to(scales[:, :, None], (rows, groups, 32))
+    return tl.reshape(scales, (rows, groups * 32))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _mxfp8_gemm(
+    Act,
+    ActScale,
+    Weight,
+    WeightScale,
+    ExpertScale,
+    Out,
+    Tiles,
+    MAX_CTAS: tl.constexpr,
+    N: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    TILE: tl.constexpr,
+    BN: tl.constexpr,
+    BT: tl.constexpr,
+    BK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    T_BLOCKS: tl.constexpr = tl.cdiv(TILE, BT)
+    tl.extra.cuda.gdc_wait()
+    pid_t = tl.program_id(1)
+    tile = pid_t // T_BLOCKS
+    if tile >= tl.load(Tiles + 2 * MAX_CTAS):
+        return
+    expert = tl.load(Tiles + tile).to(tl.int64)
+    row_end = tl.load(Tiles + MAX_CTAS + tile)
+    rows = tile * TILE + (pid_t % T_BLOCKS) * BT + tl.arange(0, BT)
+    row_mask = rows < tl.minimum(row_end, (tile + 1) * TILE)
+    cols = tl.program_id(0) * BN + tl.arange(0, BN)
+    col_mask = cols < N
+    weight = Weight + expert * N * K
+    weight_scale = WeightScale + expert * N * (K // 32)
+    acc = tl.zeros((BN, BT), tl.float32)
+    for k in range(0, K, BK):
+        kp = k + tl.arange(0, BK)
+        kg = k // 32 + tl.arange(0, BK // 32)
+        w = tl.load(
+            weight + cols[:, None].to(tl.int64) * K + kp[None, :],
+            col_mask[:, None],
+        )
+        w_scale = _expand_scales(
+            tl.load(
+                weight_scale + cols[:, None] * (K // 32) + kg[None, :],
+                col_mask[:, None],
+            )
+        )
+        a = tl.load(
+            Act + rows[:, None].to(tl.int64) * K + kp[None, :],
+            row_mask[:, None],
+        )
+        a_scale = _expand_scales(
+            tl.load(
+                ActScale + _scale_offsets(rows[:, None], kg[None, :], K // 32, TILE),
+                row_mask[:, None],
+            )
+        )
+        acc = tl.dot(
+            _dequant_e4m3(w, w_scale), tl.trans(_dequant_e4m3(a, a_scale)), acc
+        )
+    acc = acc * tl.load(ExpertScale + expert)
+    tl.store(
+        Out + rows[None, :].to(tl.int64) * N + cols[:, None],
+        acc.to(tl.bfloat16),
+        row_mask[None, :] & col_mask[:, None],
+    )
+
+
+def bmm(
+    act: torch.Tensor,
+    act_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    row_scale: torch.Tensor | None,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    ones: torch.Tensor,
+    tiles: torch.Tensor,
+    plan: ExpertPlan,
+    projection: int,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Multiply quantized expert rows, returning bf16 `[plan.rows, N]`."""
+    del projection
+    if weight.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+        n, k = weight.shape[1:]
+        assert k % 128 == 0
+        if plan.tile <= 16:
+            block_n, block_t, num_warps = 128, 16, 4
+        elif plan.tile <= 64:
+            block_n, block_t, num_warps = 128, 64, 4
+        else:
+            block_n, block_t, num_warps = 256, 128, 8
+        out = torch.empty((plan.rows, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=act.device)
+        _mxfp8_gemm[
+            (triton.cdiv(n, block_n), plan.max_ctas * triton.cdiv(plan.tile, block_t))
+        ](
+            act,
+            act_scale,
+            weight,
+            weight_scale,
+            ones,
+            out,
+            tiles,
+            MAX_CTAS=plan.max_ctas,
+            N=n,
+            K=k,
+            TILE=plan.tile,
+            BN=block_n,
+            BT=block_t,
+            BK=128,
+            num_warps=num_warps,
+            num_stages=3,
+            launch_pdl=True,
+        )
+        return out
+    assert weight.dtype == torch.uint8
+    n, k = weight.shape[1], weight.shape[2] * 2
+    block_m, block_n, num_warps = 32, 64, 4
+    if plan.tile >= 128 and n == 2304 and k in (1152, 2304):
+        # Mini's prefill tiles reuse each weight load across more routed rows.
+        block_m = 128
+        block_n = 128 if plan.tile >= 256 else 64
+        num_warps = 8
+    out = torch.empty((plan.rows, n), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=act.device)
+    _expert_gemm[
+        (plan.max_ctas, triton.cdiv(plan.tile, block_m), triton.cdiv(n, block_n))
+    ](
+        act,
+        act_scale,
+        row_scale,
+        weight,
+        weight_scale,
+        ones,
+        out,
+        tiles,
+        MAX_CTAS=plan.max_ctas,
+        N=n,
+        K=k,
+        TILE=plan.tile,
+        BM=block_m,
+        BN=block_n,
+        BK=512,
+        num_warps=num_warps,
+        num_stages=2,
+    )
+    return out
